sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: A rosette succulent with leaves about 25–50 cm long. Plants reach around 0.6 m, with horticultural profiles giving spreads up to 1 m. Flowering clusters can reach 90 cm and bear greenish-yellow tubular flowers. Kew places its native range in Oman’s Hajar Mountains; it is widely cultivated elsewhere.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The clear inner-leaf gel is used in some food products. The yellow latex beneath the leaf skin can cause abdominal pain, cramps and diarrhoea; whole-leaf extracts are not equivalent to purified gel. The leaf should not be described as wholly edible.
